thread:
maya: heads up - Acme reported p99 spikes (3000ms -> 9s) on text-generation route after the 03:00 deploy :grimacing:
escalations-bot: alert: route=/v1/generate tenant=acme p99=9000ms p95=1200ms count=2500 window=5m
alex: any repro or logs? can you attach a sample request or pattern?
maya: they said high cardinality of 'conversation_id' headers + short TTL on prefixcache. saw correlation with sudden card spike at 03:05. cc @jamal
jamal: looking at traces now. p50 ~200ms, p95 ~1.2s, p99 jumps when kv miss rate > 40%. pattern: many uniques like session tokens appended to prefix -> ineffective caching.
jamal: quick metric dump:
```
kv.prefix_miss_rate{tenant=acme} = 0.52
kv.evictions/sec = 180
cache.size.used = 78%
inflight.batch_size.p50 = 1
```
tanya: fetching eviction logs from warmup pool... one snippet:
```
[03:04:58] evict key=prefix::conv:abcd1234 ttl=2s reason=ttl-expire
[03:04:58] insert key=prefix::conv:efgh5678
[03:04:59] evict key=prefix::conv:efgh5678 reason=capacity
```
lee: confirmed small TTLs + high cardinality -> churn. Also seeing header-key explosion: X-Client-Session contains full uuid in prefix.
alex: probable root: earlier change to reduce memory by aggressively low TTLs and no jitter. when traffic has many unique session ids stash misses cause eviction storm + backend spike.
maya: customer timeline: steady until 03:00 deploy, then progressive p99 climb and occasional 5xx timeouts. they throttled and saw reduced errors but p99 still high.
jamal: repro steps I used:
1) replay 10k requests/sec with unique conversation ids (uuid suffix) for 5m
2) set prefix TTL=2s
3) observe evictions/sec surge and p99 above 6s
command:
```
ab -n 10000 -c 200 -H "X-Conversation: conv-$(uuidgen)" http://staging.redwood/v1/generate
```
results: p99 jumps after ~30s of sustained unique keys.
tanya: suggested mitigations (short term):
- increase prefix TTL to 30s for that tenant
- add jitter to TTL +-20% to avoid synchronized expirations
- normalize/remove volatile header parts (strip uuid) in prefix keying
- enable admission control to coalesce unique-key bursts
alex: long term:
- implement consistent prefix hashing + shard affinity to avoid cross-shard evict storms
- per-tenant soft reservations (spillover cache quota)
- improve key canonicalization rules in SDKs/docs
maya: can we push a quick hotfix: set TTL override for Acme -> 30s and enable TTL jitter?
lee: I can push TTL override via feature-flag for tenant acme now. will monitor for 10m. rolling change: `curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/tenants/acme/cache-override -d '{"prefix_ttl":30,"ttl_jitter":0.2}'`
alex: also enable verbose kv metrics for Acme for next 15m (`kv.debug=on`) to confirm miss patterns.
jamal: I'll keep a replay running on staging to validate the fix prevents p99 climb. will post numbers in 5m.
maya: customer notif draft: "We've identified cache churn caused by high-cardinality session keys. Pushing a temporary TTL increase and jitter to stabilize latency; we'll follow up with key normalization guidance and a permanent fix."
lee: TTL override applied at 03:10 UTC. initial telemetry: kv.miss_rate -> 0.18, evictions/sec -> 22, p99 -> 640ms
jamal: reproducer run shows steady p99 < 800ms under unique-key load now. looks good.
maya: thanks team. next steps: create a ticket to add header-canonicalization rules in SDK and prod rollout for jittered TTL defaults. I'll update the customer and close once they ack. :thumbsup:
